dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies with authority to enter into other transaction agreements, the Department of the Treasury, the OMB, agency Inspectors General, and the Government Accountability Office.
dimensions.evidence: each agency described in paragraphs (1) and (2) of section 901(b) of title 31, United States Code

dimensions.assessment: Requires federal agencies and the Treasury to change reporting practices, automate data transmission, and publish annual reports on unreported funding.
dimensions.evidence: ensure that data relating to other transaction agreements is automatically transmitted to the website

dimensions.assessment: Involves tracking and reporting federal spending on other transaction agreements and unreported funding, but does not specify total appropriation amounts.
dimensions.evidence: the total amount of Federal spending on Federal awards for which data has not been posted to the website

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 to alter definition and reporting standards for federal awards.
dimensions.evidence: amends the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 to ensure that other transaction agreements are reported

dimensions.assessment: Imposes ongoing annual reporting and sets oversight and Inspector General reporting requirements for a duration of 10 years.
dimensions.evidence: until the date that is 10 years after the date of enactment of the Stop Secret Spending Act of 2025

missing_information: Dollar amounts of other transaction agreements previously omitted from public tracking
Cost to federal agencies of implementing automated data transmission
importance_detail.rationale: The bill broadens transparency requirements by mandating that other transaction agreements be reported on USAspending.gov, establishes agency reporting and quality controls, and requires periodic Inspector General and Comptroller General reports over a ten-year span.
